summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR320 crores (+24% YoY) and EBITDA crossed INR100 crores for the first time at a 31.9% margin, led by Healthcare (+78% YoY).
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY and 14% QoQ to INR320 crores, the highest ever quarter, with EBITDA of INR102 crores (31.9% margin) and PAT of INR61 crores (+20% YoY). Healthcare became the largest segment at 55% of revenue, while Consumer stayed about 14% below last year and was flat QoQ, which management called stabilisation. Management said West Asia freight and polymer costs and weak European and US home-furnishing demand shaped the quarter, and it prioritised margin over Consumer volume. Management also said the 25 million pen capacity starts qualification next week and could sell from December.

financial_highlights.metric: Debt to equity / fixed asset turnover

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR175 crores (+78% YoY), 55% of revenue vs 38% a year ago; H1 INR318 crores (+81%). Growth led by pen injectors for GLP-1 programs, with steady insulin volumes. 10.4 million devices delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR116 crores, down 14% YoY and flat QoQ; H1 INR231 crores, down 19% YoY. Management expects the segment to hold at this level through FY27.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR29 crores, up 23% YoY (INR23 crores a year ago); H1 INR51 crores, up 24%. Growth from automotive, appliances and consumer electronics; 7 new power tool products and new knobs confirmed by an appliance customer.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to exceed the FY27 device guidance of 36 million; the exact amount was not quantified and the next call will update it.
FY28 pen volume target of about 15% growth on the 50 million figure raised by an analyst; management said this is not formal guidance.
Abu Dhabi facility is expected to be ready by end FY28 (confirmed by management).
Consumer business is expected to be flat for FY27, with growth possible in FY28 depending on geopolitics.
Consumer Electronics and Semiconductor Packaging scale-up is expected over the next 36 months; the capex minimum is about INR100 crores, possibly INR80-120 crores.
Management expects to maintain Healthcare margins because of pricing indexation and expected operating leverage; the UK subsidiary is expected to be EBITDA and PAT positive for the full year.
capex_capacity: 25 million pen capacity added; qualification starts next week, with commercial sales from December if all goes well.
Second line (Neo line) installed and entering qualification the week after the call.
Machine utilisation rose to 52.5% in Q2 from 47.8% a year ago; management said significant operating leverage is yet to kick in.
Semiconductor trays are to begin commercial shipments in Q4 FY27 from the existing facility; trial production starts Q3 FY27.
Consumer Electronics: commercial supplies have started, with production of 5 awarded components being scaled; initial capex is about INR100 crores.
Eye applicator completed qualification and is expected in supply by end of Q2 or early Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Healthcare average revenue per device rose to about INR168 from INR158 QoQ, which management attributed to mix: GLP-1 replaced contract insulin manufacturing at higher realisations.
Pricing pressure of 10-15% in pens was previously flagged; price erosion is built into long-term contracts, and an index mechanism passes through material inflation.

Semaglutide generics launched in India in March, Canada approved a generic in April, and Brazil approved its first generic in August. Shaily has approval in Brazil and Canada and claims close to 100% share in Canada.
Export share of revenue was 62.9% in H1 FY27 vs 71.7% in H1 FY26, as Indian pharma customers serve global markets.
Insulin is being deprioritised behind GLP-1; management expects insulin to recover next year. Pen volume split is about 70:30 GLP-1 to other by year-end.
Toby Reusable (2-step reusable auto-injector) launched at CPHI; about 80% development complete and a partner is being sought. Claimed 70% more sustainable than a disposable two-step device.

Semiconductor: targeting JEDEC trays, carrier tapes and wafer boxes via a Korean partner with 150+ global customers; contract manufacturing and exports to Korea/Taiwan planned. Management expects margins above Consumer and Industrial averages but not price-competitive with Malaysian and Chinese players.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Ministry of Health recall (dose display and labelling issues) affect Shaily, and does Toby Reusable cannibalise existing products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recall relates to a pen variant with an incorrect label carried by another party's assembly or packaging, with nothing attributed to Shaily, and that demand is strong. It said Toby Reusable targets innovators and does not cannibalise the existing portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for on-body Mira and emergency auto-injectors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is close to finalising a customer for on-body Mira, followed by a 14-month path to clinical batches. Toby Emergency has 2 active customers, with clinical batches due end CY27 and commercialisation around end CY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will healthcare guidance be revised, and what is FY28 volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 will exceed 36 million, with the amount not yet known, and ramp-up pressure is still easing. For FY28 it is targeting about 15% growth on the 50 million base, which is not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 45% QoQ, and is the UK subsidiary loss-making?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of one-off costs and higher expenses from business mix, and declined to quantify the one-offs. The subsidiary loss was attributed to unrecognised revenue pending customer confirmations; management expects full-year EBITDA and PAT positive for the UK subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Consumer Electronics capex and when will semiconductor business scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said initial capex is about INR100 crores, possibly INR80-120 crores, and that it is too early to discuss higher figures. Semiconductor trial production starts Q3 FY27 with commercial shipments in Q4.

risks_watch: Healthcare ramp-up pressure: management said it is still work in progress and has not eased.
Pricing erosion in GLP-1 pens (10-15% flagged) and whether margin holds without operating leverage at 52.5% utilisation.
Consumer demand in Europe and the US remains weak; management expects the segment flat in FY27.
Recall-related questions on labelling and dose errors at other companies' products; management says no impact but it remains a headline risk.
The UK subsidiary is loss-making in H1 and depends on unrecognised revenue being confirmed.
Consumer Electronics and Semiconductor capex (about INR100 crores) and customer ramp timing; the cost of Toby Reusable development and its partner search.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Healthcare growth and on exceeding the device guidance, but cautious and non-committal on FY28 volumes, Consumer recovery and the size of the Consumer Electronics capex. Management was evasive on quantifying one-off other-expense costs and on the ramp-up timeline.
key_quotes: This is the first time we have crossed the INR100 crores EBITDA milestone in a single quarter.
We will exceed the guidance. Now how much we exceed it by, I have no clue.
So it's a combination of one-off expenses and some increase in expenses.
I'd say we will maintain our margins primarily because there's no operating leverage that has kicked in yet.
